sources.title: Muse Wonder: A Frontier Model For Personal & Professional AI Agents
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The October 12 announcement explicitly compares Spark 1.3 with Wonder Full and attributes the Wonder models' gains to larger, stronger base models. It covers pretraining and reinforcement learning but supplies neither a nominal total nor an active-parameter count for Full; its comparison axes measure task performance, not parameter counts.

sources.title: Muse Wonder Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 and checked the complete 13-page card, including the visual benchmark table on PDF page 3. The shared specification explicitly names Wonder and Wonder Full, Meta, October 12, text/image/video/audio input, text output and 1M context. Full evaluations use max effort, with xhigh for SWE-Marathon. There is no total/active-parameter specification or parameter-count comparison column.

sources.title: Models - Meta Model API
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The availability table identifies Full as a distinct higher-capability variant available only in Muse Code on Power Usage and Maximum Usage subscriptions. Max effort on ordinary Wonder does not select Full. The precise 1,048,576-token limit and PDF input appear in the ordinary Wonder API description. No Full parameter count is given.

sources.title: Muse Wonder | Meta
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The Full-specific product block and muse-wonder-full-1.0 pricing row list 1M context and subscription-only Muse Code access. The page associates Full with Active Memory and Active Focus and separately labels Wonder/Full benchmark columns; these contain scores, not total or active counts.

sources.title: Put your ideas to work with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The October 12 launch confirms Full is exclusive to Muse Code subscriptions and describes series reasoning, sequential tool invocation, error recovery, coding, multimodal understanding, Active Memory and Active Focus. It has no parameter disclosure or named numerical base-model specification for Full. Audio support on a particular release surface requires separate confirmation.

sources.title: Meta Model API Terms of Service
sources.evidence: The October 9, 2026 terms cover coding-harness subscriptions as well as model services. They grant limited access/use rights and retain service ownership for Meta or its licensors; separate open-weight licenses are distinct. Together with Full-only subscription distribution, this supports a proprietary classification.

sources.title: Muse Spark Open Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The October 15 model card specifies 816B total, 42B active and MoE Transformer for Muse Spark Open. Its comparison tables have no Wonder or Wonder Full entry. It does not establish either Full count; the additional PyTorch lineage sources identify Spark models, while the Wonder announcement describes larger bases.

sources.title: Models.dev Muse Wonder Full record
sources.evidence: The upstream comment explains that its 1,048,576 context number expands the card’s 1M using other Muse documentation. It also notes Full has no API reference and that ordinary Wonder API format lists do not establish Full input formats. Used to trace the baseline assertion, not verify it.

sources.title: Muse Spark Is Now an Open-Weights Model
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. The October 15 post specifies Spark Open at 816B total/42B active, says it builds on the August Spark release with additional safety post-training, and shares Spark 1.3's base. It contains no Wonder/Full mention, count or shared-base statement.

sources.title: TorchTitan Update: New SOTA Models, Performance at Scale, TitanRL
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. The Muse Spark Open section identifies the release as MuseSpark 1.2 OSS and discusses training infrastructure. It supplies no Wonder/Full parameter count or lineage relationship; the Spark-specific disclosure cannot establish Full's size.

sources.title: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI — original interview transcript
sources.publisher: Cheeky Pint; statements by Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. In the October 12 launch interview, Meta's leaders identify Wonder and Wonder Full as two models, call Full higher-end, and describe the Wonder class as significantly larger than Spark. Wang explicitly distinguishes their pretrains. The transcript contains no total or active parameter count; general scaling-step remarks do not quantify Full.

developer.note: The provider is Meta Platforms, Inc. or Meta Platforms Ireland Limited.

family.note: Normalized Muse family grouping; Full belongs to the Wonder series.

release_date.note: Both dated announcements state that Full is available that day.

open_weights.note: Official distribution is exclusive to Muse Code subscriptions, with no Full weight release.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted subscription model under Meta service terms; no open-weight license is assigned to Full.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no nominal Full total or explicitly sized base for a lineage inference. Meta describes larger Wonder bases and a different pretrain from Spark. The new 816B Spark Open lineage evidence therefore does not quantify Full. Exact-name parameter searches across Meta research/developer sources, PyTorch and arXiv found no later disclosure.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no Full active-parameter count, routing specification or original research-team comparison with a Full-specific activated-parameter column. The current visual comparison table reports benchmark scores only. Spark Open's published 42B active count belongs to a different pretrain and cannot be transferred to Full.

architecture.note: Pretraining/RL and larger base models do not specify production architecture. Targeted training/interpretability searches found no Full-specific structural disclosure; Spark Open MoE is separate.

context_window.note: Nominal 1M, explicitly scoped to Full in its product row and shared card. The exact Full token ceiling is not disclosed; 1,048,576 belongs to ordinary Wonder documentation and was transferred by the catalog.

modalities.note: Shared card explicitly covers Full. These are model modalities, not confirmed Muse Code file formats or direct audio-upload support. PDF is not imported from ordinary Wonder API docs.

reasoning.note: Full evaluations explicitly use reasoning effort. Full is a separate model, not an effort setting on the ordinary API model.

tool_call.note: The series capability description explicitly includes sequential tool invocation and recovery from failed calls.

description.value: Meta's multimodal reasoning model for coding, computer use and tasks involving tools, available through Muse Code subscriptions. Full is a separate variant from the Muse Wonder API model.
description.note: Concise supported capabilities and Full-specific subscription access; removes promotional labels while retaining the model-identity distinction.

patch.notes: Full is subscription-only in Muse Code, not the ordinary Wonder API model at high or max reasoning effort. Context is the published nominal 1M; an exact Full limit of 1,048,576 is not established. Model-card audio modality does not establish direct audio support on every release surface, and PDF support is not transferred from ordinary Wonder API documentation. Full total/active parameters and architecture remain undisclosed. Meta describes larger Wonder bases and a separate pretrain from Spark, so Spark Open's 816B total/42B active counts do not establish Full's size.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts with explicit null patches. Reopened the Wonder/Full card and visual comparison table, launch, product/API documentation and Spark Open card; checked the later PyTorch release/infrastructure posts and original Meta leadership interview. New evidence establishes Spark-specific lineage and separate, larger Wonder pretraining, not a numerical Full specification. No Full-specific activated-parameter comparison was found. The other twelve field assessments are unchanged.
